nodes.label: RULINGS-R4f.md
nodes.author: M
nodes.rationale: The twelve rulings on the entry point, the field readings and the residue, plus ruling 13; successor to RULINGS-R4e.md.

nodes.label: Ruling 1 — the entry-point form is a floor
nodes.rationale: t(ℓ) = √(ℓ(ℓ+1)/2) carries a one-signed excess growing with ℓ (+4.04 % at p, +5.37 % at d), six of six measured openings above the form, so the volume states it as a floor approached from above.

nodes.label: Ruling 2 — lanthanum's 5d reading is an R3 correction
nodes.rationale: The printed 5d entry point was read from the first ionisation energy, which removes a 6s electron; the La II 6s² ¹S₀ limit at 52,376 cm⁻¹ gives t = 1.8049 against the printed 1.7240.

nodes.label: Ruling 3 — register 1337's 'no f test' corrected
nodes.rationale: False under the g ruling: 5f has a two-sided corridor and the f test now exists, so 1337 is corrected by a new appended entry citing it.

nodes.label: Ruling 4 — nothing accepted without complete residue closure
nodes.author: M
nodes.rationale: M: 'nothing is accepted without evidence and verification of complete residue closure.' A bracket is not evidence and residue is not closure; W-101's 'completely true and proven' applied to the 5f figure. Discharged in full at 6.95 eV (range 6.94–7.05), t(5f) = 2.636.

nodes.label: Ruling 8 — all three recorded limits are work
nodes.rationale: M: 'they must be repaired, worked, and then verified/proven completely' — not recorded and left.

nodes.label: Ruling 8(a) — the g_2b quadrature, repaired and converged
nodes.rationale: The 1 % was a limit of what the chat export carried, not of the record: recovered/sox_qres.py is the snapshot from before the record's own numerical fix. The repair reproduces gate (51)'s sealed golden with nothing fitted and costs the object ≤ 0.005 mHa.

nodes.label: Ruling 8(b) — the spin–orbit ζ, worked and bounded
nodes.rationale: Not repaired, and the reason is measured: the potential is immaterial, the exchange projection moves the wrong way, and the Koelling–Harmon factor leaves d at 1.22–1.33 while destroying p — at least two faults of opposite sign. It costs the object nothing (0.019 eV at protactinium against ±0.11 eV already carried).

nodes.label: Ruling 8(c) — t7c_cuaudit.py settled as absent
nodes.rationale: The absence is explained rather than observed — the record's route leads to a second absent file and neither name is in COVERAGE.tsv, so no wanted-set run of recover.py can reach either. Seven of the module's eight interface names are pinned by a held file and the eighth, v_gbz, by a held implementation of itself; the status stays RECONSTRUCTED and is never flattened.

nodes.label: Ruling 12 — where two true statements differ only in reach, take the more expanded
nodes.author: M
nodes.rationale: M: 'always the most expanded answer, in this case the wider bound.' Stated as a general rule, not only as a decision about §35's g-block bound.

nodes.label: The two-body spin–other–orbit term (Blume–Watson)
nodes.rationale: Built on M's 'build it'. For a closed core the term has no direct part — the Hartree average needs Σ⟨s⟩ or the net orbital current and both vanish — so the entire effect is exchange. The angular reduction was derived, not looked up, and validated at six independent levels; two real faults were caught by those checks.

nodes.label: The noded-orbital limitation at 3p and 4p shells
nodes.rationale: Blume & Watson paper II reports both the exact theory and ⟨∂V/r∂r⟩ lying below experiment for 3p and 4p shell atoms, explained by the noded nature of the outer radial wave functions — the same shells where the residual appears here, with nothing fitted to it. The d-row half stays open.

nodes.label: Correlation scales with actual sibling count, not a closed shell's share
nodes.rationale: Ytterbium's 4f¹⁴ carries thirteen pairs where protactinium's 5f² carries one, so a residual measured on nearly-full f shells does not transfer to a nearly-empty one. Confirmed a third time by the ion-relaxation subtraction: +2.7 % at Pa against +59 % at Yb.

nodes.label: The R4 order of work — test, repair, then the R3 corrections
nodes.rationale: Rulings 4 and 8 are testing and repair rather than recording, so they move to the front; the R3 corrections rulings 2, 3, 9, 10, 11 and 12 authorise come third, under docs/R3-REPAIR-PLAN.md's mechanic.
